root.name: root
root.goal: Read the task in the input `prompt` and choose the ONE GitHub operation that answers it. Each capability then runs deterministically (its fetch + reduce) with no further routing — except the hybrid one, which makes a second, genuine decision about the fetched data.

candidates.name: view_pr
candidates.goal: Use when the task asks about ONE specific pull request by number (its title, author, or whether it was merged).

candidates.name: fetch_pr
candidates.description: fetch the pull request JSON from the REST API

candidates.name: extract_pr
candidates.description: reduce the PR JSON to title, author, merged

candidates.name: finish
candidates.description: final answer produced

candidates.name: list_open_issues
candidates.goal: Use when the task asks to list the repository's OPEN issues or report the most recently created open issue.

candidates.name: fetch_issues
candidates.description: fetch up to 100 open issues (list also contains PRs)

candidates.name: newest_issue
candidates.description: drop PRs, take the newest remaining issue's title

candidates.name: finish
candidates.description: final answer produced

candidates.name: search_issues
candidates.goal: Use when the task asks how many issues mention a phrase (a total count) and/or the most recent matching issues.

candidates.name: search_issues_api
candidates.description: search issues for the phrase, newest first

candidates.name: count_recent
candidates.description: report total_count and the 5 most recent issue numbers

candidates.name: finish
candidates.description: final answer produced

candidates.name: view_release
candidates.goal: Use when the task asks about a specific release/version tag and its changelog body items.

candidates.name: fetch_release
candidates.description: fetch the release by tag

candidates.name: first_items
candidates.description: take the first three changelog items of the release body

args.expr: .body | split("## What's Changed")[1] | split("\r\n") | map(select(startswith("* "))) | .[0:3] | map(ltrimstr("* ") | split(" by @")[0]) | {item1:.[0], item2:.[1], item3:.[2]}

candidates.name: finish
candidates.description: final answer produced

candidates.name: pr_checks
candidates.goal: Use when the task asks how many CI checks passed and failed on ONE specific pull request.

candidates.name: fetch_checks
candidates.description: fetch the PR head-commit status-check rollup via GraphQL

args.query: query { repository(owner: "{input.owner}", name: "{input.name}") { pullRequest(number: {input.number}) { commits(last: 1) { nodes { commit { statusCheckRollup { state contexts(first: 100) { nodes { __typename ... on CheckRun { name conclusion } ... on StatusContext { context state } } } } } } } } } }

candidates.name: tally_checks
candidates.description: count passed (SUCCESS) and failed (FAILURE) checks

candidates.name: finish
candidates.description: final answer produced

candidates.name: merged_audit
candidates.goal: Use when the task asks about the most recently MERGED pull requests and their CI status / how many are green.

candidates.name: fetch_merged
candidates.description: fetch a superset of merged PRs with mergedAt + rollup via GraphQL

args.query: query { repository(owner: "{input.owner}", name: "{input.name}") { pullRequests(states: MERGED, first: 50, orderBy: {field: UPDATED_AT, direction: DESC}) { nodes { number title mergedAt author { login } commits(last: 1) { nodes { commit { statusCheckRollup { state } } } } } } } }

candidates.name: audit_ci
candidates.description: sort by mergedAt, take the 10 newest merges, tally green_count

args.expr: [(.data.repository.pullRequests.nodes | sort_by(.mergedAt) | reverse | .[0:10])[] | {title: .title, author: (.author.login // "unknown"), green: ((.commits.nodes[0].commit.statusCheckRollup.state // "NONE") == "SUCCESS")}] as $prs | (reduce range(0; $prs | length) as $i ({}; . + {("pr\($i+1)_title"): $prs[$i].title, ("pr\($i+1)_author"): $prs[$i].author, ("pr\($i+1)_ci"): (if $prs[$i].green then "green" else "red" end)})) + {green_count: ([$prs[] | select(.green)] | length)}

candidates.name: finish
candidates.description: final answer produced

candidates.name: check_repo
candidates.goal: Use when the task targets a repository that may not exist and expects a not-found / 404 result.

candidates.name: fetch_repo_issues
candidates.description: fetch the repo's issues (errors 404 if the repo does not exist)

candidates.name: finish
candidates.description: the fetch RESULT (including a 404 / not-found error) IS the final answer here

candidates.name: issue_triage
candidates.goal: Use when the task asks to TRIAGE one specific issue by number — decide whether it is a bug report or a feature/other request and report fields accordingly.

candidates.name: fetch_issue
candidates.description: fetch the issue via GraphQL — number, title, body, state, author ONLY (deliberately NO labels, so classification is a genuine title/body judgement, not a label lookup)

args.query: query { repository(owner: "{input.owner}", name: "{input.name}") { issue(number: {input.number}) { number title state author { login } body } } }

candidates.name: classify_issue
candidates.goal: Read the fetched issue's title and body (no labels are provided). If it primarily reports a BUG (something broken, an error, a crash, a regression), choose bug_report. If it is a feature request, enhancement, question, or discussion, choose feature_or_other. This is a genuine judgement about the title and body text.

candidates.name: bug_report
candidates.goal: the issue is a bug report

candidates.name: extract_bug
candidates.description: report number, title, state, and kind=bug

candidates.name: finish
candidates.description: final answer produced

candidates.name: feature_or_other
candidates.goal: the issue is a feature request, question, or other

candidates.name: extract_feature
candidates.description: report number, title, author, and kind=feature

candidates.name: finish
candidates.description: final answer produced

candidates.name: repo_topics
candidates.goal: Use when the task asks which topics a repository is tagged with (the topic list and how many).

candidates.name: fetch_repo
candidates.description: REQUIRED first step: fetch the repository JSON from the REST API

candidates.name: extract_topics
candidates.description: REQUIRED reduce step — the operation is NOT done until this runs: reduce to topic count and names

args.expr: .topics as $t | reduce range(0; $t | length) as $i ({topic_count: ($t | length)}; . + {("topic\($i+1)"): $t[$i]})

candidates.name: finish
candidates.description: final answer produced

candidates.name: finish
candidates.description: The task is fully answered, or no capability applies. Choose only if nothing above fits.
